newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia sets rules for sale of Ventspils terminal.
newsitem.headline: Latvia sets rules for sale of Ventspils terminal.

text.p: Latvia's privatisation agency has set the rules for the sale of oil terminal company Ventspils Nafta and pipeline operator Lasam which will take place in four stages, the agency said on Wednesday.

After the privatisation process, the capital of Ventspils Nafta, a major outlet for Russian crude oil, will rise from 30 million lats to around 200 million lats and the state will be left with 26 percent of the shares, agency legal director Viktor Shadinov told Reuters.
He said the new rules still have to be finally confirmed by the agency's board, which would take place in around two weeks.
He said the four stages involve the sale of the state's 90 percent stake in Lasam, the Latvian partner in the LatRosTrans firm, which operates the oil pipeline on Latvian territory.
The current minority Lasam shareholders, several companies involved in the oil transit business in Lasam, will have first refusal on the state's shares.

The second stage will involve the merger of Lasam with Ventspils Nafta, the third step will be the sale of shares in the merged Lasam/Ventspils Nafta in a mix of public offers and placements abroad while the fourth stage is the sale of seven percent of Ventspils to Lasam shareholders.
Shadinov said 15.5 percent of the company would be sold in the public offer.
"We plan to have the first stage of the public offer for July," Shadinov said.
A second stage would take place in September or October.
Some five percent of the shares will be sold for cash, seven percent will be placed abroad and two percent will be placed with state-owned Savings Bank as part of its restructuring.
He also said 0.75 percent will be distributed between employees and 0.75 percent to the current management.
The sale of the seven percent in the fourth stage will be carried out according to the price of Ventspils shares on the stock exchange, where the shares will be quoted after the public offer.
